- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5–10 days.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% for next 5–10 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent high for 3–5 days.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish within 3–5 days, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in next 5–7 days.
- Model underestimates mean-reversion periods (e.g., after 3–5 consecutive days of high prices); add 1–3% upward bias for 3–5 days if sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often misses early trend reversals; if sentiment turns negative after 10–15 days, reduce forecast by 3–7% for next 5–10 days.
- If sentiment is negative and price is falling, model often forecasts a steeper decline; adjust downward by 1–3% per day if sentiment remains negative for >3 days.
